record.title: Duncan–Steingrímsson's bistatistic equidistribution conjecture for 021-avoiding ascent sequences
record.statement: An ascent sequence of length $n$ is a nonnegative integer sequence $x=x_1x_2\ldots x_n$ with $x_1=0$ and $x_i\leq \operatorname{asc}(x_1x_2\ldots x_{i-1})+1$ for $1<i\leq n$, where $\operatorname{asc}(x_1x_2\ldots x_{i-1})$ is the number of ascents in the prefix. Let $\mathcal{A}_n(021)$ be the set of ascent sequences avoiding the pattern $021$, and let $S_n(132)$ be the set of permutations in $S_n$ avoiding $132$. For a sequence $x$, let $\operatorname{rlm}(x)$ be the number of right-to-left minima, meaning indices $i$ such that $x_i<x_j$ for every $j>i$. **Duncan–Steingrímsson's conjecture.** The bistatistic $(\operatorname{asc},\operatorname{rlm})$ has the same distribution over $\mathcal{A}_n(021)$ and $S_n(132)$. This refines the known equidistribution of the ascent statistic alone and relates two Catalan families; the source provides no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: William Y. C. Chen, Alvin Y. L. Dai, Theodore Dokos, Tim Dwyer and Bruce E. Sagan, “On 021-Avoiding Ascent Sequences”, arXiv:1206.2849 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.2849

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2012).

record.title: Kozlov's non-evasiveness conjecture for order complexes
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset with an element $s$ such that

1. for all $x
e P$, either $s\vee x$ or $s\wedge x$ exists; and
2. for all $x,y\in P$ such that $x<y$, if $s\wedge x$ does not exist but $s\wedge y$ does exist, then $(s\wedge y)\vee x$ exists.

**Kozlov's conjecture.** The order complex of $P$ is non-evasive.

The conjecture concerns a combinatorial strengthening of contractibility for order complexes. It is proved in the paper, so the conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Jonathan David Farley, “A Conjecture of Kozlov from the 1998 Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society: Non-Evasive Order Complexes and Generalizations of Non-Complemented Lattices”, arXiv:2201.01491 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.01491

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The divisibility conjecture for $T_y(j)$ in normal mixed Cayley graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group, let $y\in\Gamma(3)$, and suppose that $S_y^2$ exists. For $1\leq j\leq h$, let $T_y(j)$ be the character sum defined from $S_y^2$ by

$$
T_y(j)=\frac{1}{\chi_j(1)}\sum_{s\in S_y^2}\sqrt{3}\,i\bigl(\chi_j(s)-\chi_j(s^{-1})\bigr).
$$

**The divisibility conjecture.** For every $1\leq j\leq h$,

$$
\frac{T_y(j)}{3}\in\mathbb{Z}.
$$

The source notes that this divisibility holds for abelian groups and for $A_4$, while the general finite-group case is presented as a conjecture and remains open.
record.source_name: Monu Kadyan, “HS-integral and Eisenstein integral normal mixed Cayley graphs”, arXiv:2201.08160 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.08160

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: Grothendieck support poset conjecture
record.statement: Let $w\in S_n$, and let $\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w)$ be the set of exponent vectors of the nonzero terms of the Grothendieck polynomial $\mathfrak{G}_w$. For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{Z}^n$, write $\alpha\leq\beta$ when $\alpha_i\leq\beta_i$ for every $i\in[n]$; write $\alpha<\beta$ for strict componentwise comparison. **Grothendieck support poset conjecture.** If $\alpha\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w)$ and $|\alpha|<\deg\mathfrak{G}_w$, then there exists $\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w)$ with $\alpha<\beta$. The paper proves this for fireworks permutations, but the assertion for arbitrary permutations remains open.
record.source_name: Karola Mészáros, Linus Setiabrata and Avery St. Dizier, “On the support of Grothendieck polynomials”, arXiv:2201.09452 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09452

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: Interval-closed support conjecture for Grothendieck polynomials
record.statement:
Let $w\in S_n$, and let $\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w)$ be the set of exponent vectors of the nonzero terms of $\mathfrak{G}_w$. Order $\mathbb{Z}^n$ by componentwise comparison: $\alpha\leq\beta$ if $\alpha_i\leq\beta_i$ for every $i\in[n]$. **Interval-closed support conjecture.** If $\alpha,\gamma\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w)$, then

$$
\{\beta\in\mathbb{Z}^n\mid\alpha\leq\beta\leq\gamma\}\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w).
$$

The paper proves this for Grassmannian permutations, while the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Karola Mészáros, Linus Setiabrata and Avery St. Dizier, “On the support of Grothendieck polynomials”, arXiv:2201.09452 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09452

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: Top-support coefficient-sum conjecture for Grothendieck polynomials
record.statement:
Let $w\in S_n$ and write

$$
\mathfrak{G}_w=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}^n}C_{w\alpha}x^\alpha.
$$

Let $\mathfrak{G}_w^{\mathrm{top}}$ denote the top-degree part of $\mathfrak{G}_w$, and order exponent vectors componentwise. **Top-support coefficient-sum conjecture.** For every $\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w^{\mathrm{top}})$,

$$
\sum_{\alpha\leq\beta}C_{w\alpha}=1.
$$

The statement connects the componentwise support poset with Grothendieck-polynomial coefficients; it remains open in general.
record.source_name: Karola Mészáros, Linus Setiabrata and Avery St. Dizier, “On the support of Grothendieck polynomials”, arXiv:2201.09452 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09452

record.title: Ohsugi–Tsuchiya gamma-nonnegativity conjecture for symmetric edge polytopes
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mathcal{P}_G$ be its symmetric edge polytope. Write $\gamma(\mathcal{P}_G)=(\gamma_0,\gamma_1,\ldots)$ for the $\gamma$-vector associated with the palindromic $h^*$-vector of $\mathcal{P}_G$.

**Ohsugi–Tsuchiya conjecture.** For every $i\geq 0$,

$$
\gamma_i(\mathcal{P}_G)\geq 0.
$$

This conjecture extends gamma-nonnegativity from flag simplicial spheres to symmetric edge polytopes, whose relevant triangulations need not be flag. The supplied status evidence says that this instance was proved in the original work of Hibi, Matsuda, and Murai and generalized by Ohsugi and Tsuchiya to the indicated bipartite-graph setting; it is therefore solved.
record.source_name: Alessio D'Alì, Martina Juhnke-Kubitzke, Daniel Köhne and Lorenzo Venturello, “On the gamma-vector of symmetric edge polytopes”, arXiv:2201.09835 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09835

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2022). “This last instance was originally proved in but was generalized in to bipartite graphs $\widetilde{H}$ obtained from another bipartite graph $H$ as in .”

record.title: Up-elbow bound conjecture for bumpless pipe dreams
record.statement: Let $\omega$ be a permutation, and let $P\in\operatorname{Pipes}(\omega)$. If $P$ is non-reduced, replace the redundant crossings with bump tiles. **Up-elbow bound conjecture.** Pipe $i$ has at most $r_{\omega^{-1}(i)}-c_{\omega^{-1}(i)}$ up-elbows, including the up-elbow portions of any bump tiles. This generalizes the proved bound for vexillary permutations to arbitrary permutations; the source gives no resolution of the general case.
record.source_name: Elena S. Hafner, “Vexillary Grothendieck Polynomials via Bumpless Pipe Dreams”, arXiv:2201.12432 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.12432

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

record.title: The chain-of-triangles bound for expected faces
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n$, and let $F$ denote the number of faces of a uniformly random orientable embedding of $G$. **Chain-of-triangles conjecture.** For every such graph,

$$
\mathbb{E}[F]\leq \frac{1}{3}n+1.
$$

A chain of triangles connected by cutedges attains $\mathbb{E}[F]=\frac{1}{3}n+1$, so the conjecture proposes that this construction is extremal. The source first establishes the general upper bound $\mathbb{E}[F]<\frac{\pi^2}{6}n$ for simple graphs, leaving the sharper constant conjectured here.
record.source_name: Jesse Campion Loth and Bojan Mohar, “Expected number of faces in a random embedding of any graph is at most linear”, arXiv:2202.07746 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.07746

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: The semicompleteness characterization for graph products of abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite graph with vertex groups $G_1,\ldots,G_n$, where each $G_i$ is an abelian group, and let $G_\Gamma$ be their graph product. The graph $\Gamma$ has a **separating star** if the complement of the star of some vertex is disconnected.

**Semicompleteness characterization.** The graph product $G_\Gamma$ is semicomplete if and only if $\Gamma$ has no separating star.

The statement extends the result established in the paper for finitely generated abelian vertex groups to arbitrary abelian vertex groups. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Philip Möller and Olga Varghese, “A note on semicompleteness of graph products of abelian groups”, arXiv:2202.10083 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.10083

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: Gabow's sequential symmetric exchange conjecture for matroid bases
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $r$, and let $A$ and $B$ be bases of $M$. An ordering of a basis is a listing of its elements, so write

$$
A=(a_1,dots,a_r),\qquad B=(b_1,\dots,b_r).
$$

**Gabow's conjecture.** There are orderings $A=(a_1,\dots,a_r)$ and $B=(b_1,\dots,b_r)$ such that

$$
\{a_1,\dots,a_i,b_{i+1},\dots,b_r\}
$$

and

$$
\{b_1,\dots,b_i,a_{i+1},\dots,a_r\}
$$

are bases for every $i=0,\dots,r$.
This is the sequential symmetric exchange property, equivalently expressible through a cyclic ordering in which both bases form intervals and every $r$ cyclically consecutive elements form a basis. The conjecture concerns whether the extreme case of Gabow's symmetric-exchange decomposition can always be achieved.
record.source_name: Kristóf Bérczi and Tamás Schwarcz, “Exchange distance of basis pairs in split matroids”, arXiv:2203.01779 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01779

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2022). “Despite being the center of attention not only in combinatorial optimization but also in algebra due to its connection to toric ideals and Gröbner bases , White's conjecture remains open even for sequences of length two.”

record.title: The Backman–Baker–Yuen consistency conjecture for regular matroids
record.statement: Let $M=(E,\mathcal B,\chi)$ be an oriented regular matroid, let $(\sigma,\sigma^*)$ be a pair of acyclic circuit and cocircuit signatures, and let $\alpha_{(M,\sigma,\sigma^*)}$ be the Backman–Baker–Yuen matroidal sandpile torsor action on the bases $\mathcal B$. The action is called **consistent** if it satisfies the stated contraction and deletion compatibilities for every regular matroid, every such signature pair, every basis $B\in\mathcal B$, and every $f\in E$. **Backman–Baker–Yuen consistency conjecture.** The Backman–Baker–Yuen matroidal sandpile torsor algorithm is consistent. The paper notes that the proposed matroidal consistency definition may need adjustment, so this conjecture remains open in the stated framework.
record.source_name: Ankan Ganguly and Alex McDonough, “Rotor-Routing Induces the Only Consistent Sandpile Torsor Structure on Plane Graphs”, arXiv:2203.15079 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15079

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2022). “This conjecture was independently proven by Ding as well as by Shokrieh and Wright . } However, both algorithms satisfy , and they both define the same sandpile torsor algorithm .”

record.title: Costa–Morini–Pasotti–Pellegrini restricted rotational sequencing conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group and let $S$ be a finite subset of $G\setminus\{0\}$ such that

$$
\Sigma S=0
$$

and $|S\cap\{x,-x\}|\leq1$ for every $x\in G$. **Costa–Morini–Pasotti–Pellegrini conjecture.** Then $S$ has a rotational sequencing. This weaker conjecture than the main strong sequenceability conjecture is sufficient for some applications to Heffter arrays; the supplied status evidence does not resolve it.
record.source_name: Simone Costa, Stefano Della Fiore, M. A. Ollis and Sarah Z. Rovner-Frydman, “On Sequences in Cyclic Groups with Distinct Partial Sums”, arXiv:2203.16658 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.16658

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2022). “Friedlander, Gordon and Miller conjectured the rotational sequenceability version in 1978 and this was recently resolved by Alspach, Kreher and Pastine .”

record.title: Borel CSP complexity dichotomy conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a finite relational structure, and let $\mathrm{CSP}_B(\mathcal{D})$ denote the set of codes for Borel structures admitting Borel homomorphisms into $\mathcal{D}$. The projective pointclasses $\mathbf{\Pi}^{1}_{1}$ and $\mathbf{\Sigma}^{1}_{2}$ classify the complexity of such sets.

**Borel CSP dichotomy conjecture.** For every $\mathcal{D}$, the set $\mathrm{CSP}_B(\mathcal{D})$ is either in $\mathbf{\Pi}^{1}_{1}$ or is $\mathbf{\Sigma}^{1}_{2}$-complete.

The source says that this dichotomy follows assuming $\mathbf{\Sigma}^{1}_{2}$-determinacy, but whether it holds in ZFC is open. It is intended as a descriptive-set-theoretic analogue of the finite CSP dichotomy.
record.source_name: Riley Thornton, “An algebraic approach to Borel CSPs”, arXiv:2203.16712 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.16712

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2022).

record.title: The single-row root-at-minus-one conjecture for permutation pattern character polynomials
record.statement:
Let $\sigma\in S_k$, and let $a_\sigma^\lambda(n)$ denote the polynomial associated with the stable irreducible-character coefficient for the pattern $\sigma$. A partition $\lambda$ has a **single row** when it is of the form $(r)$.

**Single-row root-at-minus-one conjecture.** When $\lambda$ has a single row, the polynomials $a_\sigma^\lambda(n)$ have $n=-1$ as a root.

The conjecture is supported by proofs for the cases $a_{\textnormal{id}_k}^{(1)}$ and $a_{\textnormal{id}_k}^{(2)}$, and by numerical verification for all patterns of size at most four. The source notes that related cases do not all satisfy the same property, so the precise single-row scope is essential.
record.source_name: Christian Gaetz and Laura Pierson, “Positivity of permutation pattern character polynomials”, arXiv:2204.10633 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.10633

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: Toroczkai's independent-edge conjecture for prime gap graphs
record.statement:
Let $p_n$ denote the $n$-th prime number, with $p_0=1$. A **prime gap graph** on $n$ vertices is a simple graph whose vertex degrees are $p_1-p_0,\dotsc,p_n-p_{n-1}$; two edges are **independent** when they have no common vertex. **Toroczkai's independent-edge conjecture.** In every prime gap graph on $n$ vertices, there exist

$$
\frac{p_{n+1}-p_n}{2}
$$

independent edges. The supplied context does not state whether this assertion has been proved or remains open.
record.source_name: Péter L. Erdős, Gergely Harcos, Shubha R. Kharel, Péter Maga, Tamás R. Mezei and Zoltán Toroczkai, “The sequence of prime gaps is graphic”, arXiv:2205.00580 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00580

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Definite symmetric determinantal representation from Rayleigh differences
record.statement: Let $f\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$ be multiaffine in $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, with nonzero coefficient of $x_1\cdots x_n$. For indices $i,j$, let $\Delta_{ij}(f)$ denote the corresponding Rayleigh difference. **Definite symmetric determinantal representation conjecture.** Some power of $f$ has a definite real symmetric determinantal representation if and only if, for all $i,j$, $\Delta_{ij}(f)$ is a sum of squares in $\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$. This is presented as a hoped-for partial converse to a known result relating definite determinantal representations to sums of squares; its resolution is not given in the source.
record.source_name: Abeer Al Ahmadieh and Cynthia Vinzant, “Determinantal representations and the image of the principal minor map”, arXiv:2205.05267 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.05267

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2022). “This conjecture was resolved by Oeding .”

record.title: Characteristic-sequence conjecture for transitive permutations
record.statement:
Let $f$ be a transitive permutation in the symmetric group $S_n$. For each $i=1,\ldots,n-1$, set $A_i=\{i,i+1\}$ and define its characteristic number by

$$
m_i=\min\{m\mid (\operatorname{conv}f)^m(A_i)\supseteq A_i\},
$$

where, for finite $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, $\operatorname{conv}f(A)$ is the convex hull of $f(A)$. Let $m_1'\leq\cdots\leq m_{n-1}'$ be the rearrangement of the numbers $m_1,\ldots,m_{n-1}$.

**Characteristic-sequence conjecture.** For every transitive $f\in S_n$,

$$
m_i'\leq i,\qquad i=1,2,\ldots,n-1.
$$

The paper states that this formulation is equivalent to the discrete conjecture above, but the supplied text does not resolve it.
record.source_name: Yihan Wang, “On an existence problem of periodic points in intervals whose images cover themselves”, arXiv:2205.07225 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.07225

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: CMPP conjecture on sequenceability with no opposite pair
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group and let $A$ be a finite subset of $G\setminus\{0\}$. A subset is **sequenceable** if it admits an ordering whose partial sums are distinct, except that the initial and final partial sums may coincide.

**CMPP conjecture.** If

$$
|A\cap\{x,-x\}|\leq 1
$$

for every $x\in G$, then $A$ is sequenceable.

This is a weaker version of the Alspach–Liversidge conjecture, presented by Costa, Morini, Pasotti, and Pellegrini for applications to Heffter arrays. The source notes that the earlier formulation included the additional hypothesis $\Sigma A=0$; the paper uses the stated slightly more general version, and does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Simone Costa and Stefano Della Fiore, “Weak Sequenceability in Cyclic Groups”, arXiv:2205.12017 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.12017

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

record.title: Weak CMPP conjecture for abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $t$ be a positive integer, let $G$ be an abelian group, and let $A$ be a finite subset of $G\setminus\{0\}$ with $|A|>t$. An ordering of $A$ is a **$t$-weak sequencing** if its partial sums $s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_{|A|}$ satisfy $s_i\ne s_j$ whenever $i\ne j$ and $|i-j|\leq t$; $A$ is **$t$-weak sequenceable** if it admits such an ordering.

**Weak CMPP conjecture.** If

$$
|A\cap\{x,-x\}|\leq 1
$$

for every $x\in G$, then $A$ is $t$-weak sequenceable.

This is the weak-sequenceability analogue of the CMPP conjecture, proposed after the paper states the corresponding general weak sequenceability conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Simone Costa and Stefano Della Fiore, “Weak Sequenceability in Cyclic Groups”, arXiv:2205.12017 (2022).
record.references:
